artworks.title: Athena and Enceladus
artworks.description: Attic black-figure amphora from Vulci: Athena closes on the Giant Enceladus in the Gigantomachy — the earthborn who will be crushed beneath Sicily, not the icy moon that later borrowed his name.

artworks.title: Artemis and Enceladus (Temple E metope, Selinus)
artworks.description: Classical metope from Temple E at Selinus: Artemis spears the falling Giant — Enceladus in stone combat, the Gigantomachy carved for a Sicilian temple that stands over the myth's volcanic ground.

artworks.title: Fountain of Enceladus
artworks.description: Marsy's gilded-lead Giant writhes under rock in the Versailles bosquet — Enceladus buried as at Etna, water standing in for volcanic fire. Photographed by Eugène Atget for the Cleveland Museum of Art.

artworks.title: Trojans Land Near Mount Etna; Beneath Lies the Giant Enceladus
artworks.description: Limoges enamel plaque (Metropolitan Museum): the Trojans beach under Etna while the Giant Enceladus lies crushed beneath the mountain — Virgil's etiology of Sicilian fire cast in Renaissance enamel.

artifacts.title: Athena and Enceladus
artifacts.description: Attic black-figure: Athena spears the Giant Enceladus as the Gigantomachy turns — the earthborn who will be crushed under Sicily.

popCulture.title: Enceladus (Giant)
popCulture.description: The Giant Athena buried under Sicily became an etiological story for Etna's fire — Enceladus still breathing under the volcano in later poets.

popCulture.title: Enceladus
popCulture.description: Saturn's icy moon took the Giant's name — Enceladus in the Cassini images, a namesake that carries the Gigantomachy into modern astronomy.
